_: The scoring model's weights (ml/training/reward.py). Data, not code, so
tuning needs no engine work (canon directive 4). Both consumers read this:
league.fitness() ranks ES candidates with it and ppo.py pays it as the
terminal reward, so the two can no longer optimise different things.
RULES ENFORCED ON LOAD (assert_sane_weights), not merely intended:
* the weights must sum to 1.0, so a score is always on a [0,1] scale
and a threshold means the same thing twice;
* 'win' must EXCEED the sum of all the others, so no amount of damage,
health or clock can make a lost episode outrank a won one.
DIRECTIONS are declared in reward.py::TERMS and are Ricardo's wording:
win / dmg_dealt / hp_self  -> higher is better
dmg_taken / hp_foe         -> lower is better
duration                   -> shorter winning, longer losing, draw neutral
WHY dmg_dealt OUTWEIGHS dmg_taken, deliberately and asymmetrically: they
used to be one symmetric term (ppo.py's hp delta, weight 1.0 each way), and
a symmetric trade means not-being-hit pays exactly as well as hitting. That
is the avoidance local optimum, and it is not hypothetical here — PPO seed 7
produced precisely that policy (mean_loser_hp 0.967, a timeout win).
model: 'v2' = the weighted model above; 'v1' = the original
league.fitness_v1 (wins + 0.1 * hp margin), kept so historical ES
rankings can be reproduced rather than only described.
